# This Week on the Northern Rivers

**Flood Watch Newsletter, Week of 11 to 17 August**

Hello everyone,

Here is your weekly update on the rivers across northern Pakistan, covering the Indus, Jhelum, Neelum, Kunhar, Poonch, and Siran. Most of our rivers are behaving themselves this week, but there is one spot worth paying attention to.

**The short version:** Out of 13 river points we keep an eye on, twelve are safe. One of them, Bunji on the Indus, has crept above its alert level, and two others on the same river are climbing too. Nothing dangerous, but a good week to stay informed if you live near the upper Indus.

## Worth Paying Attention To

**Bunji on the Indus River, above the alert level**

The Indus at Bunji has nudged just past the alert mark. Levels are expected to be at their highest on Wednesday, 13 August, and will then start easing off through the rest of the week. We are not looking at dangerous flooding, but the river will stay slightly elevated for a few days.

If you live near here, stay off the riverbank, especially with children. Keep an emergency bag handy just in case, and tune in to local announcements.

**Shatial Bridge and Besham Qila on the Indus River, rising but still safe**

Both of these points further down the Indus are still flowing within safe limits, but the water is climbing. Shatial Bridge is expected to briefly touch its alert level around 14 to 15 August before settling back down. Besham Qila stays below alert in the expected forecast, but could come close if the weather turns wetter than predicted.

No action is needed for now. It is just worth knowing if you are in these areas.

## All Clear Elsewhere

These rivers are flowing normally this week with no concerns: the Poonch at Kotli, the Jhelum at Chakothi, Chattar Kalass, Domel, and Hattian Bala, the Neelum at Muzaffarabad and Dudhnial, the Kunhar at Kaghan and Talhata Bridge, and the Siran at Phulra.

## For Local Authorities

If you are in district administration or disaster response, three things this week. First, coordinate monitoring across the three upper Indus points, Bunji, Shatial Bridge, and Besham Qila, as the high water moves downstream. Second, get the word out to communities living close to the Indus banks in the affected districts. Third, share daily updates with AJK and KPK disaster management teams through the 17th.

## What the Risk Levels Mean

Safe means the river is flowing normally with no flood danger. Watch means the river is higher than usual, so stay alert. High Risk means the river is dangerously high and flooding is likely. Emergency means severe flooding, and you should move to safety now.

Stay safe out there. We will be back next week with another update.

*The FLARE Flood Watch Team*
